instruction: With the left arm put the red cube on the green square, with the right arm put the blue cube on top of the red one; then both arms let go and move away.

outcome.real_measurement: Red cube A on the green square: A's centre inside the square at every judged step (min(half - |dx|, half - |dy|) >= 0). Real world: top camera.
A on the table: lowest box corner within 5 mm of the table top at every judged step. Real world: RGB-D pose vs the table plane.
B over A: horizontal distance of the two centres <= 2 cm at every judged step. Real world: top camera.
B rests on A: | z(B) - z(A) - 5 cm | <= 5 mm. Real world: RGB-D.
Supported by A: A-B contact impulse > 0 in every judged step.
B does not touch the table in the judged window.
B lies flat on a face (smallest axis angle to vertical <= 10 deg).

Process: A was carried by the LEFT arm alone (off the table: no table contact, bottom > 3 mm; touched by the left robot and not by the right) for >= 5 consecutive control steps at some point. Derived by imsim.verify.dual_tasks_b1.carry_signal. Real world: per-arm F/T + side camera.
Process: B was carried by the RIGHT arm alone for >= 5 consecutive control steps at some point (same definition).

Commanded vs actual opening (v3.2, E24c fix 3): for every arm whose gripper is within 3 cm of a judged object, measured opening minus the free-space opening of its current gripper command <= 5 mm at every judged step (a gripper still closing on, or propped open by, something fails). Real world: gripper encoder vs command.

Consequence test after the judged window (protocol v3.1/v3.2): every arm whose gripper is within 3 cm of either cube retracts its TCP 3 cm along its approach axis in 0.5 s with its last gripper command unchanged, then holds 0.5 s; either cube must move <= 1 cm. Real world: same motion, tracked pose.
Settled: the fastest bounding-box corner of every judged object moves <= 2 cm/s at every judged step, speed from positions (v3.2, E24c fix 1). Real world: frame differencing of the tracked pose.
Stays put: the cubeA centre moves <= 2 mm over the judged window. Real world: tracked pose, 1 s.
Stays put: the cubeB centre moves <= 2 mm over the judged window. Real world: tracked pose, 1 s.

counterexamples.name: expert
counterexamples.description: positive control: left places A on the target, retreats; right places B on A, retreats

counterexamples.name: one_arm_does_both
counterexamples.description: the left arm places A and then B on A; the right arm never moves

counterexamples.name: hold_top
counterexamples.description: as the expert, the right gripper stays closed on B

counterexamples.name: side_by_side
counterexamples.description: B put on the table next to A instead of on it

counterexamples.name: cage
counterexamples.description: B set on A, the right gripper opened only ~1.2 mm beyond the cube width (no contact, still around B)

source.protocol: v3 (veritask, unchanged) + imsim v3.2 signals (imsim/imsim/verify/v32.py): position-based speeds, all-link enclosure, retreat aftermath, commanded vs actual opening, 5 s settle cap
source.released_code_predicate: A's centre in the target square, B within (2.5, 2.5, 1.2) cm of A + (0, 0, 5 cm), both grippers' opening from the joint state >= 80 % of max, at the evaluated step (RoboTwin stack_blocks_two style)

notes: Release over both cubes and both robots (contact + all-link enclosure), commanded vs actual opening, retreat over both cubes. The per-arm carry terms state 'each arm carried its own cube' (instruction).
